The line $l_{1}: y=k_{1}x+b$ intersects the x-axis at point $(-3,0)$. What is the solution set of the inequality $k_{2}x<k_{1}x+b<0$ with respect to $x$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} From the graph, it is known that the intersection point of line $l_{1}$ and line $l_{2}$ is ($-1$, $-2$), and on line $l_{1}$, $y$ decreases as $x$ increases.\\
Since $y=k_{1}x+b$ intersects the $x$-axis at the point ($-3$, $0$), the solution set of the inequality $k_{2}x < k_{1}x+b$ with respect to $x$ is $x<-1$,\\
therefore, the solution set of the inequality $k_{2}x < k_{1}x+b < 0$ with respect to $x$ is $-3<x<-1$,\\
hence, the answer is: $\boxed{-3<x<-1}$.

The inequality k1x+b<0 means l1 is below the x-axis; since l1 intersects the x-axis at x=-3 and descends to the right, l1 being below the x-axis corresponds to x>-3.
